title: Technology Sector Update for 07/17/2018: CSOD,MDSO,IQ,ADSK

Technology stocks continued to build on their earlier gain Tuesday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 rising over 0.7% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has jumped out to a nearly 1.4% increase.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Cornerstone OnDemand ( CSOD ) was more than 5% higher late in Tuesday trading, staying within close range of its session high, that followed analysts at Piper Jaffray raising their stock rating for the software-as-a-service company to Overweight from Neutral and increasing their price target for the company's stock by $14 to $60 a share.
In other sector news:
+ Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was ending little changed Tuesday afternoon, drifting north from a more than 1% mid-morning decline, following a broadcast report the smartphone chipmaker could walk away from its proposed takeover of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) unless Chinese authorities sign off on the transaction by July 25. When Qualcomm resurrected its $43 billion bid for the rival semiconductor manufacturer in May, it set the tentative deadline to coincide with NXP Semi announcing its fiscal Q2 financial results. But now, with the deal barely hanging on life support, Qualcomm is ready to finally scrap the deal as its prospects for picking up the final regulatory approval needed for the acquisition to move forward have ebbed and waned with state of U.S./China trade relations, according to CNBC reporter David Faber. NXP Semi shares were down less than 1% in late trading.
+ iQIYI ( IQ ) was almost 1% higher Tuesday afternoon, erasing an more than 5% decline earlier in the session, after the Chinese online entertainment said it has completed its buyout of Skymoons and Chengdu Skymoons Digital Entertainment. iQIYI paid RMB1.27 billion, or about $189.8 million, for the mobile games developer as well as a conditional RMB730 million payment as Skymoons reaches certain performance milestones over the next two years. In addition to mobile games, Skymoons also has existing deals for the development and promotion of films, anime and comics.
- Autodesk ( ADSK ) has pared a portion of its more than 1% decline Tuesday afternoon that followed the software company late Monday disclosing plans to register 340,769 shares of its common stock issued to a dozen shareholders affiliated with Autodesk's July 3 acquisition of Assemble Systems. The shareholders includes a handful of institutional investors - Built Environmental Innovation Fund, Redhouse Associates and Satterfield Investments - along with other Assemble Systems insiders. The shares being registered include shares held by Computershare in escrow to fund potential indemnification obligations, and once registered, can be sold by the shareholders at their discretion.
